J.P. Morgan forecasts 300,000–400,000 US-made humanoids by 2030

Reuters reported on November 12 that J.P. Morgan expects US humanoid production to reach 300,000–400,000 units by 2030 and approximately 1.5 million by 2035, with manufacturing, logistics and warehousing leading adoption. These are forecasts, not actual output. Public reporting does not clearly identify the totals as annual or cumulative.

Humanoids Daily ↗12 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1

An industry forecast

Reuters reported on November 12 that J.P. Morgan expects US humanoid production to reach 300,000–400,000 units by 2030 and approximately 1.5 million by 2035, with manufacturing, logistics and warehousing leading adoption. These are forecasts, not actual output. Public reporting does not clearly identify the totals as annual or cumulative.

Supply and intelligence constrain deployment

The bank identifies hands, actuators, AI intelligence, training data, compute and production capacity as constraints. Most US manufacturers outside Tesla target 10,000–30,000 units annually. Factory targets therefore need to be distinguished from proven customer-site capability.

Cost claims need their assumptions

J.P. Morgan estimates costs are approaching labor parity and multishift operation could save roughly $100,000 annually per customer. Published reporting does not fully disclose robot-price or wage assumptions. Thai operators can use the forecast to frame supply and cost questions, rather than as a guarantee of returns for their own installations.
